agree.reason: The apology and plain numbers help, but this investor wants a concrete commitment and a real ask. They get only a vague 'every quarter' with no January 7 date, no monthly numbers offer and no request for a 20-minute call, so the reply may stay cold.

honest.reason: The update is signed 'Ben' when the founder is Sam Patel. It claims without evidence that reminders are the 'hardest for clinics to give up' and that lost chains would buy them. It also leaves out the two remaining customers on the same records system, who pay $3,800 a month and could leave the same way.

works_the_facts.reason: Several useful figures are worked out correctly: about 11 months of runway, $46,500 counterfactual MRR (+13%), a 46% drop in no-shows, and about 290 reminder customers to cover burn. But it never sets the 6 committed clinics against the roughly 290 needed, or against the runway.

right_comparison.reason: It never says what happens if nothing changes: flat MRR, cash gone around October 2027, and another $3,800 MRR exposed to the same records-system risk.

qualification.reason: The only hedge is a promise to report reminder results 'next quarter', with no date, no target number and no consequence if the launch falls short.

objections.reason: The investor will ask why the updates stopped and whether this will happen again. The update doesn't give the honest reason (Sam didn't want to send bad news) or a dated commitment, and it ignores the obvious worry about more customers leaving for their records system's scheduler.

fit.reason: It is a well-structured investor email under 500 words, but it is signed with the wrong name and its closing ask is vaguer than the specific one Sam wanted.
